verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. It validly establishes that any real orthogonal matrix with no nonzero fixed vector has determinant (-1)^n, computes det(H) = -1, and obtains det(HQ) = (-1)^(n+1). If HQ had no nonzero fixed vector, the determinant-parity observation would instead force det(HQ) = (-1)^n, a contradiction. The statement is self-contained, all hypotheses are used, and no prohibited or unverifiable citations occur.
